text:
michelle: Heads-up — saw a reproducible spike in duplicate calls from the onboarding sampleapp this morning. Root cause looks like 429s + token refresh race + SDKs having different jitter defaults. We hit prod-sim and ended up with two side-effects for a single user flow. :/
ajay: Ugh. Did you get logs? I remember a similar blip where the Go SDK was aggressively retrying without jitter while node had full-jitter.
michelle: Yep, attaching the condensed trace we pulled from staging: `TRACE: req=abc123 status=429 retry=1 token_refresh=true idempotency_key=none` then another `req=abc123 status=200 side_effect=applied` right after. We don't set Idempotency-Key in the sampleapp by default.
liam: Repro steps were simple: heavy parallel onboarding requests + short TTL on the test token service. The token refresh caused a replay window where two requests looked unique to the server.
tom: So two things: (1) ensure SDKs converge on a safe retry strategy (and default to some jitter), (2) update sampleapp to recommend/auto-add Idempotency-Key header for mutating routes.
ajay: Agreed. I sketched a small config we can propagate across SDKs (non-breaking):
```
retry:
  max_attempts: "6"
  base_backoff_ms: "100"
  max_backoff_ms: "2000"
  strategy: "decorrelated-jitter"
  idempotency: "recommended"
```
michelle: Nice. For idempotency header we should use `Idempotency-Key: {{run_id}}` and add a note in quickstart. Also add a short snippet in the sampleapp that sets it for onboarding POSTs.
liam: On the retry strategy — can we align on "decorrelated-jitter" (aka full + randomized) rather than simple exponential? It avoids synchronized retry storms. AWS blog has the summary we used before: https://www.awsarchitectureblog.com/2015/03/backoff.html
tom: Will changing defaults break any deterministic tests? We have some e2e harnesses that assert timing behaviour.
ajay: We'll make it opt-in initially via env var `RW_RETRY_MODE` and then flip the default after one release cycle. That keeps tests reproducible. I'll add a small compat flag in all SDKs.
sdk-bot: CI:lint failed on node-sdk (flake) — created ticket https://github.com/redwood-inference/node-sdk/issues/342 (auto-note).
michelle: Thanks. Can someone own updating the sampleapp + docs? If we push a minor patch to the sampleapp this afternoon we can avoid more customer confusion.
liam: I'll open the PR for sampleapp change + docs update (links to config and idempotency examples). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sampleapp/pull/789
ajay: I'll shepherd the SDK parity PRs: node (WIP), python (ready), go (needs tests). I'll add unit tests that assert the default backoff curve and that idempotency header is preserved across retries.
tom: Sounds good. michelle, ping me if you want a quick canary on staging after we merge.
michelle: Please do. Also let's add a one-line blurb in the onboarding flow about "why we set Idempotency-Key" so users don't get scared. Thanks all :thumbsup:
